content.comment_body: Hello. I'm experiencing a similar issue. I have a [product_name] connected via a switch to my PC. When I attempt to ping the device at 192.168.0.3, there is no response. However, I can see the device is present in [product_name] software. Any suggestions?

Hello [user_name], Welcome to the forum. The "[product_name]" you mentioned is just a symbolic name used in the network project. Could you specify which exact [product_name] you have? Please provide the precise [company_name] order number and firmware version. What is the PC's IP address and subnet mask? How have you connected the PC to the [product_name]? Is it direct, via a router, or a switch? Try searching for the [product_name] in your network within an empty network project (see attached video). If the software detects the device, open its properties window, take a screenshot, and share it with us.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is unable to ping a [product_name] device on their local network, although it is visible in the configuration software. Support is seeking specifics on hardware model, configuration, and clarifies that the symbolic name is not an identifier. There seems to be confusion regarding network communication and device discovery across network layers.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates being able to ping the [product_name] device at its network IP, not just access it through configuration software.
